opencode.notes: skill_path targets .opencode/commands/ rather than .opencode/skills/ as a safety property, not a preference: opencode skills are model-invoked through its native `skill` tool and have no `disable-model-invocation` equivalent, so shipping eighteen worktree-creating, branch-pushing workflows as skills would make them auto-startable. Commands are `/`-invoked only. Subdirectories under .opencode take their plural names. opencode's `write` tool is first-class alongside `edit` (verified 2026-09-13 against the shipped binary, which defines both in the same tool table alongside `bash`), and the `edit` capability maps to BOTH — `edit` alone cannot create a file.
opencode.steering_notes: No documented modular rules/instructions auto-load path; steering installs to receipt-owned `.shipmates/contributor-steering.md` — open it when contributing to Shipmates.

antigravity.notes: Antigravity CLI (agy) replaced the retired Gemini CLI (shut down June 18, 2026). Workspace agents live at `.agents/agents/{name}/agent.md` — a DIRECTORY per agent, not a flat file — with YAML frontmatter (`subagent: true`, `mainAgent: false`), skills at `.agents/skills/{name}/SKILL.md`. The CLI reads project instructions from AGENTS.md with GEMINI.md as the legacy fallback. Global scope is `.gemini/config/` (agents at `{name}/agent.md`, skills at `skills/{name}/SKILL.md`), NOT `.agents/` joined to the home directory. Verified 2026-09-13 against the shipped `agy` binary, which embeds the templates `{workspace}/.agents/agents/{agent_name}/` and `{workspace}/.agents/skills/{skill_name}/SKILL.md`.
antigravity.steering_notes: No documented modular rules/instructions auto-load path; steering installs to receipt-owned `.shipmates/contributor-steering.md` — open it when contributing to Shipmates.

codex.notes: Subagents GA March 2026. Project-scoped agents at `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` — standalone TOML, NOT Markdown with frontmatter, and the only target so far that is not. Fields: name, description, developer_instructions. Codex documents no per-agent tool allowlist, so `permission_model` is `none`: least privilege genuinely cannot be expressed on this target and the crew inherit the session's tools. Recorded rather than faked — an invented `tools` key would be ignored at best, rejected at worst. Skills follow the open Agent Skills standard at `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Codex reads `.agents/skills`, NOT `.codex/skills`); only the crew are Codex-native under `.codex/`. Verified 2026-08-03. GLOBAL SCOPE: Codex's home is `$CODEX_HOME` (default `~/.codex`), and it discovers and installs skills at `$CODEX_HOME/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — so a global install relocates the shared-tree skills out of `.agents/skills/` and into `.codex/skills/`. `.agents/skills` remains the WORKSPACE location. Crew already land at `.codex/agents/` in both scopes. Verified 2026-09-13 against the shipped codex binary's own strings.
codex.steering_notes: No documented modular rules/instructions auto-load path; steering installs to receipt-owned `.shipmates/contributor-steering.md` — open it when contributing to Shipmates.

cursor.notes: Cursor ships no subagents, so the adapter emits only the eighteen commands as skills and ignores `roles`. Cursor's slash-command picker only lists skills from its first-party `.cursor/skills/` tree, so skills ship there rather than to the shared `.agents/skills/` location (#405). One copy, not two: a second copy under `.agents/skills/` would list every command twice in the picker and double prompt cost. Verified 2026-09-12.

github-copilot.notes: Custom agents at `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` — the double extension is required; a plain `<name>.md` in that directory is never discovered. Markdown + YAML frontmatter; `tools` takes the canonical names (read, search, edit, execute, web, agent) and OMITTING the key enables every tool, so an empty mapping must never silently become an unrestricted agent. Frontmatter + body capped at 30,000 characters. Copilot accepts skills at `.github/skills`, `.claude/skills` AND the open `.agents/skills` (all first-party, since 2025-12-18), so skills ship to the shared `.agents/skills/` tree — byte-identical with codex/antigravity/cursor; only the crew are `.github`-native. Verified 2026-08-03. GLOBAL SCOPE: Copilot's configuration directory defaults to `~/.copilot` — its CLI reports "Skills are automatically discovered from: ~/.copilot/skills/" and resolves a non-project agent to `<config-dir>/agents`. A global install therefore relocates to `.copilot/skills/` and `.copilot/agents/<name>.agent.md`; `.github/` is the WORKSPACE location only. Verified 2026-09-13 against the shipped copilot package's own strings.

windsurf.notes: Windsurf (Cascade) discovers skills under `.windsurf/skills/`. It ships no subagents, so the adapter emits the crew as eighteen skills and ignores `roles`.
windsurf.steering_notes: No documented modular rules/instructions auto-load path; steering installs to receipt-owned `.shipmates/contributor-steering.md` — open it when contributing to Shipmates.

pi.notes: Pi's crew mechanic comes from the third-party `pi-subagents` extension (github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents) — core pi documents no declarative subagent schema, which is why this target once claimed `agents: false`. pi-subagents reads crew from `.pi/agents/{name}.md` (canonical project scope) and `~/.pi/agent/agents/` (user scope), and still reads the legacy `.agents/**` tree for compatibility — which is the path Antigravity's crew installs to. Shipmates emits to the project-scope `.pi/agents/`, which outranks the legacy `.agents/` tree *within whichever directory pi resolves as the project root* — the nearest ancestor carrying `.pi/` or `.agents/`. A project-local install therefore resolves correctly (the normal case). A `--global` install lands in the home directory, which is the resolved root only when no ancestor between the working directory and `~` carries `.pi/` or `.agents/`; where one does, pi reads that one and the home install is invisible. Pi's user scope cannot rescue that case: `~/.pi/agent/agents/` is loaded *before* legacy `~/.agents/` and the later write wins, so no user-scope path can outrank a foreign `~/.agents/agents/`. `tools` is a COMMA-SEPARATED SCALAR, never a YAML list: pi's frontmatter reader is line-based, so a list opens a block and is read as one unmatchable name, leaving the seat with no tools and no error (#437). `permission_model` is `allowlist` because an unresolvable name yields zero tools rather than being ignored. Skills stay on the shared `.agents/skills/` tree. Known gap: `web_search` / `fetch_content` come from a separate extension (`pi-web-access`), not pi core, so the two crew roles declaring the `web` capability name tools a bare pi install does not have. Verified 2026-09-13 against pi-subagents' own source and docs.

grok-build.notes: Native `.grok/` tree, not the shared `.agents/skills/` one, for a safety property: the eighteen commands ship `disable-model-invocation`, and only the native rendering keeps it — the neutral shared rendering emits the Agent Skills standard's `name`/`description` pair alone and would drop the guard. Grok also scans the `.agents/` and `.claude/` trees, but resolves `.grok/` ahead of both. Crew are a flat `.grok/agents/{name}.md` — Markdown + YAML frontmatter, camelCase for multi-word keys, `name` and `description` required. `tools` is a COMMA-SEPARATED SCALAR of Claude-compatible tool names resolved through Grok's first-party alias table: only a name that resolves to a real tool kind is retained, which is why the adapter emits nothing but alias-legal names (Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash, WebSearch, WebFetch) — an unresolvable entry silently reverts the seat to the FULL toolset, so a made-up name widens privilege instead of narrowing it. `permission_model` is `allowlist` on that basis. `allowed-tools` is parsed into the harness's own skill record and shown in its extensions UI, but no code path applies it as a permission filter (source-verified 2026-09-20), so the adapter drops it rather than imply a boundary that does not exist. RECORDED GAP: the toolbox cannot be model-invoked while hidden from the `/` menu — the key that removes a skill from invocation also removes it from the model's — so tool skills ship typeable, exactly as they do on cursor, codex, github-copilot and pi. GLOBAL SCOPE: a project-level `.grok/`, `.agents/`, `.claude/` or `.cursor/` skill tree outranks User scope (`~/.grok/skills`), so a `--global` install can be shadowed by any ancestor project tree; install into the project. No `global_root` key: the workspace-shaped `~/.grok/...` paths are already correct joined to home.
